subject: Physics
scope_summary: Imported candidate for Fluid Statics & Dynamics, Archimedes & Bernoulli. No authority is carried; every gap below must be authored before this can be admitted.

microtopics.title: Fluid Statics & Dynamics, Archimedes & Bernoulli
entry_assumptions: **Incompressible & Non-Viscous Fluid Invariant**: Bernoulli's equation $P + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 + \rho g h = \text{const}$ strictly applies **along a streamline** for an ideal fluid (incompressible, non-viscous, irrotational, steady flow).

**Archimedes Principle Buoyant Force Invariant**: Buoyant force equals the weight of the *displaced* fluid volume: $F_b = \rho_{\text{fluid}} V_{\text{submerged}} g$. It acts through the center of buoyancy (centroid of displaced volume).
microtopics.inferential_jump: Hydrostatic pressure variation with depth: $P = P_0 + \rho g h$. Pascal's principle: pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished.

teaching_path.action: Bernoulli's conservation of energy per unit volume along a streamline: $P_1 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v_1^2 + \rho g y_1 = P_2 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v_2^2 + \rho g y_2$.

Torricelli efflux analysis: (1) Apply continuity between tank surface and small orifice, (2) Neglect surface descent speed ($v_1 \approx 0$), (3) Equate surface pressure to orifice pressure ($P_0$), (4) Deduce $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.
Venturi meter pressure differential analysis: $\Delta P = \frac{1}{2}\rho (v_2^2 - v_1^2) = \rho_{\text{manometer}} g \Delta h$.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assuming that water rushing fast out of a nozzle has high internal static pressure.
misconceptions.repair: By Bernoulli's principle, an increase in fluid velocity along a horizontal streamline occurs alongside a *drop* in static pressure.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Claiming a 1 kg lead sphere and a 1 kg aluminum sphere experience the same buoyant force in water.
misconceptions.repair: Buoyant force depends strictly on *displaced fluid volume*, not object mass. Since lead is denser, its volume is smaller, so it experiences less buoyant force than aluminum.
